name: CBR-DDI (Case-Based Reasoning Enhances the Predictive Power of LLMs in Drug-Drug Interaction)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2505.23034, cs.AI; submitted 29 May 2025). Also submitted to ICLR 2026 and presented at the XLLM-Reason-Plan workshop (July 2025) per OpenReview id Ylf5t1j4Yu; no peer-reviewed acceptance confirmed as of mid-2026.
authors_affiliation: Guangyi Liu (Dept. of Electronic Engineering, Tsinghua University), Yongqi Zhang (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Guangzhou), Xunyuan Liu (Tsinghua University), Quanming Yao (Tsinghua University; corresponding author). Lead/primary affiliation: Tsinghua University.
code_url: N/A (no official code repository is linked in the paper; no public CBR-DDI repo was located. The unrelated LARS-research/CSSE-DDI repo is a different prior project by an overlapping group) [uncertain]
task_domain: Scientific decision-making / biomedical prediction: drug-drug interaction (DDI) type prediction, framed as a reasoning/classification task for LLMs (decision-making in a scientific domain).
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, non-interactive inference. Given a query drug pair (u,v), predict the interaction type r from a fixed relation set. Two evaluation regimes for emerging/unseen drugs: S1 (one emerging drug vs. one existing drug) and S2 (two emerging drugs), plus S0 (both drugs seen) in the appendix. Supervision: ground-truth interaction labels exist in training data and are used to construct cases and to verify/revise predictions; the LLMs themselves are NOT fine-tuned (plug-and-play). A GNN module (EmerGNN-style) is trained on the biomedical KG. The knowledge repository of cases is induced offline.
what_is_retrieved: Cases: structured problem-solution units, each a drug pair enriched with (i) LLM-generated functional drug descriptions, (ii) GNN-extracted drug-association representation, (iii) an LLM-distilled interaction-mechanism explanation, and (iv) the interaction-type label. Effectively distilled pharmacological 'cases' rather than raw demos.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID. Cases are drawn from a knowledge repository induced offline from historical/training DDI data (a growing/refinable store updated via representative sampling), while drug-association facts are grounded in a STATIC external biomedical KG (HetioNet) via a trained GNN. Retrieval combines semantic (LLM-description embeddings) and structural (KG-subgraph GNN) signals.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-K case ranking (K=5 reference cases by default; K=1,5 studied in retrieval ablations). For TWOSIDES the task is cast as top-5 recommendation (Recall@5/NDCG@5); for DrugBank single-label classification. Not a minimal-set-completeness objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] - all four canonical CBR phases are implemented: Retrieve (hybrid LLM-GNN case retrieval), Reuse (dual-layer knowledge-enhanced prompting / analogical reasoning), Revise (verify prediction vs. ground-truth label and prompt revisions for errors), Retain (representative-sampling refinement and storage of revised cases in the repository).
explicit_cbr_grounding: True. The work explicitly frames itself as case-based reasoning, citing classical CBR literature (Aamodt & Plaza-style clinical CBR, Kolodner-lineage, Althoff et al. 1998, Bichindaritz & Marling 2006, Hennessy & Hinkle 1992) and motivating from clinical decision-support CBR; method named CBR-DDI.
retrieval_unit: case (problem-solution): a drug-pair case combining functional drug descriptions, KG-derived drug-association representation, distilled interaction-mechanism text, and the interaction-type label.
index_source: Hybrid offline-induced + dynamically-refined store. The case repository is constructed offline from historical/training DDI data (LLM distills mechanisms; GNN encodes associations) and is dynamically refined at use time via verification-driven revision and representative sampling. Drug-association evidence comes from a static external biomedical KG (HetioNet) through a trained GNN.
index_structure_topology: Hybrid: a case repository organized/clustered by DDI category (representative cluster centroids per interaction type via text-embedding clustering of mechanisms) backed by dense vector indices for semantic (description embeddings) and structural (GNN subgraph embeddings) similarity; drug associations sit on a knowledge-graph topology queried by an attention-based subgraph GNN.
retriever_type: Hybrid. Combines dense semantic retrieval (LLM-generated drug-description embeddings via a text embedding model, RoBERTa-style) with structural retrieval over KG subgraph representations produced by an attention-based GNN (EmerGNN). Retrieval score s(p,c)=lambda*SemanticSim + (1-lambda)*StructSim with cosine similarity.
retriever_learning_signal: Mixed. The semantic side uses an off-the-shelf text embedding model (no contrastive training reported). The structural side uses a GNN (EmerGNN) trained on the KG for the DDI task, so the structural similarity component carries downstream-task-effectiveness signal; the fusion weight lambda is a tuned hyperparameter rather than a learned policy. No RL/preference learning for retrieval.
query_construction: For a query drug pair (u,v): an LLM generates concise functional descriptions D_p=(D_u,D_v) (intent/feature extraction), embedded for semantic similarity; in parallel the GNN encodes the KG subgraph connecting u and v (using description embeddings as node features) to produce h_p for structural similarity. Both form the retrieval key.
query_granularity: Task-level / one-shot at t=0: a single retrieval is issued per query drug pair. It is a two-channel (semantic + structural) query but not multi-step or trajectory-level.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (single retrieval per query before reasoning). Not iterative or uncertainty-triggered.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per query drug pair before prompting (no confidence/attention/router trigger).
reranking: Single-stage ranking by the weighted hybrid score s(p,c)=lambda*SemanticSim+(1-lambda)*StructSim, then top-K selection; no separate cross-encoder reranking stage. Candidate interaction TYPES are separately pre-filtered to top-N by GNN scores (a form of candidate pruning, distinct from case reranking).
retrieved_context_refinement: Pre-injection refinement at two levels: (i) candidate-answer pre-filtering to top-N interaction types by GNN scores to reduce label-space noise/distractors; (ii) top-P attention-weighted relational paths selected from the GNN as high-quality factual evidence (instead of heuristic triplet retrieval). The repository itself is also distilled via representative sampling. No reason-in-documents distillation per query.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; cases are engineered by LLM-distilling interaction mechanisms and GNN-encoding associations, but this is case engineering not tool-document engineering).
index_content_separation: Partial: described as a 'lightweight' knowledge repository; representative sampling compresses the store to cluster centroids (over 90% size reduction on DrugBank), separating a compact representative set from the full case pool. No explicit progressive-disclosure index-then-content protocol.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool API/MCP/RapidAPI integration). The case repository is dynamically refined (verification + representative sampling) but not a live tool index.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling). The method does model inter-drug structural dependencies via KG relational paths, but not tools.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation via case reuse / analogical adaptation: retrieved cases' interaction-mechanism text plus GNN-extracted drug-association facts and filtered candidate types are assembled into a dual-layer knowledge-enhanced prompt; the LLM synthesizes them to produce the predicted mechanism M_p and interaction type T_p. No fine-tuning; in-context learning only.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-reason (one-shot exemplars/cases at prediction time). Retrieval feeds a single dual-layer prompt that the LLM uses to generate the mechanism explanation and interaction-type prediction; no multi-step planning, tree search, or interleaved per-step retrieval.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer: a single retrieval-and-reasoning pass produces one prediction (mechanism + type) per query drug pair.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted analogical adaptation of retrieved cases (in-context), combined with execution-/label-feedback-driven revision in the Revise step: predictions are verified against ground-truth labels and erroneous cases are revised (re-prompted with the correct label to regenerate the mechanism) before being retained.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled, structured natural-language case: free-text interaction-mechanism explanation + functional drug descriptions + structured KG relational paths (e.g., Fosphenytoin -binds-> CYP3A4 -binds-> Diphenhydramine) + candidate interaction-type label set. Injected as text in the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy/insight at the case level: generalizable pharmacological interaction-mechanism patterns abstracted from historical drug-pair cases (not raw trajectories, not single demonstrations), paired with state-aware factual evidence (drug-association paths).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Multiple guards: (i) hybrid semantic+structural retrieval to ensure retrieved cases share both functional and structural relevance; (ii) attention-weighted top-P path selection to filter low-quality KG triplets; (iii) top-N candidate-answer pre-filtering to suppress irrelevant label distractors; (iv) representative sampling to remove redundant/noisy cases from the repository; (v) verification-and-revision to correct erroneous stored cases.
memory_type: Hybrid episodic + graph: a case repository (episodic/case memory of pharmacological cases) refined dynamically, grounded by a graph (biomedical KG of drug associations encoded by a GNN).
write_back: True. New/resolved cases (with verified or revised interaction mechanisms) are written into the knowledge repository; the store is dynamically refined.
online_growth: Partial / controlled growth. The repository can incorporate new resolved cases and adapt to new discoveries, but representative sampling deliberately controls (compresses) growth; experiments evaluate on a largely offline-induced, sampled repository rather than unbounded test-time accumulation.
write_back_trigger: Reflective / on-verification: for each LLM prediction, correctness is verified against the ground-truth label (from training data or expert feedback); correct cases are retained and incorrect ones are revised (re-prompted with the correct label) before storage. Effectively on-success-and-failure with correction.
failure_experience_usage: Failures are corrected rather than stored as negatives: erroneous predictions trigger label-grounded revision so the corrected (positive) case is retained. No explicit success-vs-failure contrastive retrieval or failure-only corrective rules reported.
memory_evolution_update: Refine-overwrite + dedup-merge + forget-prune: cases are revised/overwritten upon error correction, semantically similar cases are clustered and merged to representative centroids (dedup), and redundant cases are pruned (over 90% reduction on DrugBank).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case selection is fixed similarity-based top-K (weighted hybrid score with a tuned lambda); not an RL/learned retrieval policy. The structural-similarity GNN is trained on the task but the case-selection rule itself is not a learned policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private repository. The framework is plug-and-play across different backbone LLMs (Llama3.1-8B/70B, DeepSeek-V3), but there is no cross-agent/cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: DrugBank (Wishart et al. 2018; multi-class, 86 interaction types) and TWOSIDES (Tatonetti et al. 2012; multi-label, 200 side effects). Evaluated under S1 (emerging vs existing drug) and S2 (two emerging drugs) settings; S0 (both existing) in appendix. External KG: HetioNet (Himmelstein & Baranzini 2015).
benchmark_family: Biomedical / scientific decision-making (drug-drug interaction prediction); a domain-specific benchmark family (not in the QA/web/embodied/tool/code/memory taxonomy). Knowledge-graph-grounded relational prediction.
baselines: Traditional (non-LLM): MLP, ComplEx, MSTE, Decagon, SumGNN, EmerGNN, TIGER. LM/LLM-based: TextDDI (fine-tuned RoBERTa), DDI-GPT (referenced in comparison table), Base LLM (zero-shot), Naive-CBR (fingerprint-similarity 10-shot case retrieval), K-Paths (Abdullahi et al. 2025, heuristic KG-path prompting). Backbone LLMs: Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, DeepSeek-V3-671B.
key_metrics: DrugBank: Accuracy and macro-F1. TWOSIDES (recommendation framing): Recall@5 and NDCG@5. Aggregate improvement reported as Delta_avg (average accuracy+recall improvement across the two datasets). Repository-size (#Case) reported for the sampling ablation.
headline_result: CBR-DDI achieves state-of-the-art performance with a ~28.7% accuracy improvement over the Naive-CBR baseline (and 463% over the base LLM). Best DrugBank S1 results: with DeepSeek-V3, F1=74.38 (Acc 71.05); with Llama3.1-70B, Acc=71.36 / F1=70.85, vs. strongest non-LLM baseline EmerGNN (DrugBank S1 Acc 68.10 / F1 65.78).
ablations: (1) Dual-layer knowledge augmentation (Table 3, Llama3.1-70B): full (DrugBank S1 Acc 71.4) vs w.o.case (factual-only, 68.3) vs w.o.asso (regularity/case-only, 69.4); removing either layer degrades performance, and retrieved cases (regularity) are more critical than KG associations alone. (2) Representative sampling (Table 4): cuts repository size by >90% (DrugBank S1 35,255 -> 2,139 cases) with comparable/slightly-improved accuracy (71.36 -> 71.05). (3) Hybrid retriever weight lambda (Figure 4): retrieval accuracy peaks at a balanced semantic+structural mix, confirming both channels matter. (4) Effect of #cases K and #paths P (appendix): accuracy rises then saturates/decreases with larger K/P.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial. End-to-end task metrics (Acc/F1/Recall@5/NDCG@5) are primary, but the hybrid-retriever ablation reports intrinsic retrieval accuracy (majority-label of top-K under varying lambda), decoupling retrieval quality from final task performance for that study.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final interaction-type prediction). Some process signals are examined qualitatively (case studies show retrieved cases, extracted association paths, generated mechanism explanations, interpretability) and the retrieval-accuracy ablation; no quantitative step-wise reasoning-faithfulness metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Plug-and-play, no LLM fine-tuning ('without intensive interactions'); single retrieval+single LLM call per query. Representative sampling reduces repository size by >90% (e.g., DrugBank S1 35,255->2,139 cases) improving scalability/storage with negligible accuracy change. Compute: GNN training + Llama3.1-8B inference on one RTX 3090-24GB; Llama3.1-70B on two A100-80GB; DeepSeek-V3 via API. No explicit latency/token-cost numbers reported. [uncertain] on exact token/latency cost.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k injection: K=5 reference cases, P=5 association paths, candidate answers capped at top-N (3 for DrugBank, 10 for TWOSIDES; varied among {3,5,10}). No explicit token-budget cap reported; selection is fixed-k then truncated by candidate pre-filtering.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing datasets, not a newly constructed benchmark). For reference: DrugBank split 1,461/79/161 train/valid/test drugs, 86 relations, 137,864 training edges; TWOSIDES 514/30/60 drugs, 200 relations, 185,673 training edges; HetioNet used as external KG.
builds_on: EmerGNN (Zhang et al. 2023; attention-based subgraph GNN for emerging-drug DDI, reused for structural similarity and association-path extraction); classical CBR for clinical decision support (Aamodt & Plaza lineage, Althoff et al. 1998, Bichindaritz & Marling 2006); in-context learning / few-shot prompting (Brown et al. 2020); KG-grounded DDI (HetioNet); recent CBR+LLM integration work (Wilkerson & Leake 2024; Guo et al. 2024).
contrasts_with: Naive-CBR (fingerprint-similarity case retrieval giving only labels, no pharmacological insight), K-Paths (Abdullahi et al. 2025, heuristic KG-path prompting that may inject irrelevant/redundant info), TextDDI and DDI-GPT (fine-tuned small-LM classifiers, limited LLM compatibility/interpretability), and pure GNN/feature DDI methods (EmerGNN, SumGNN, TIGER, Decagon, MSTE, ComplEx, MLP) that require task-specific training.
lineage: Group D: case-based planning / case-based reasoning lineage (explicit CBR with full Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle), applied to a scientific decision-making domain; hybrid LLM+GNN retrieval over a dynamically-refined case/experience memory grounded in a biomedical KG.
